title: Enhancement: Upgrade to libyang3
author: bradh352
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the enhancement

SONiC currently uses 3 versions of libyang: 1.0.73, 1.0.184, and 2.1.148. All are end of life and potentially have security issues. The current release is 3.12.2 and that is what we are targeting here.

There are also numerous libyang related bugs that have been "worked around" in SONiC due to the shortcomings of libyang1. Hopefully upgrading to a modern version will resolve such issues.

### Current Behavior

3 libyang versions

### Proposed Behavior

single libyang version


### PR Tracking Table

Legend: ~~strikethrough~~ = merged/done.

| ~~#24414~~ | sonic-yang-mgmt: helpers to keep dependents from calling into libyang directly |

comments.author: bhouse-nexthop
comments.body:
> [@bhouse-nexthop](https://github.com/bhouse-nexthop) , was there a community review for the set of changes that are proposed here? I am asking so that I can learn more and be able to address the review/merge concern in a timely manner. We also need to make sure that there are test cases and test coverage that validate the claims here, and ensure that no regression is added. I don't see a sonic-mgmt PR linked here, is that because it is not needed? I am assuming the issues fixed here are discovered due to your due diligence, and not due to SONiC test suite complaining. :)

Hi @vaibhavhd  the motivation is 2 fold, one is that libyang 1.0.73 has long been EOL and is therefore not receiving any security patches which is a major issue.  The second is that there are many issues with libyang v1 that the community has "worked around".  You can see a small number of those issues if you grep the `src/sonic-yang-models/yang-models` yang models themselves for "libyang" where people have documented issues in comments.

Libyang v1 -> v3 is a complete rewrite, they are not API compatible at all.  So the goal isn't to write any *new* sonic-mgmt tests, but rather to ensure *existing* sonic-mgmt tests continue to work to validate the porting effort was successful.

The primary patch that has had community review is the sonic-mgmt-common patch, which is pretty large and written in Go lang with cgo.  The other 2 largest patches have already been merged (#21679, #21719).  The rest will be fairly small in comparison.

I'm in the process of reworking the patch series to be easier to apply.  My original series here has some cross-dependency things going on where you'd actually have to merge things in parallel, which would mean manual intervention would be needed to pass the submodule updates which isn't friendly.  It will still likely be *order* dependent but not require any special privileges.  (Not to mention that so much time has passed that some areas of the patch series have to be completely reworked due to merge conflicts and significant code changes).

If we can coordinate *quickly* we can get this done without too much pain, hopefully before the 202511 cutoff, but it will likely be a couple of dozen PRs across a dozen submodules with the new reworked approach.

The next patch in the series is available *now* for review and merge: #24414

comments.author: ganglyu
comments.body:
@bradh352 

Thank you very much for your contribution!

We have encountered numerous issues with libyang 1.0.73, which is currently used by sonic-yang-models. On the other hand, libyang 1.0.184 and libyang 2.1.148, which are used by FRR, have not presented any issues to our knowledge.

comments.author: bradh352
comments.body:
@ganglyu 
> @bradh352
> 
> Thank you very much for your contribution!
> 
> We have encountered numerous issues with libyang 1.0.73, which is currently used by sonic-yang-models. On the other hand, libyang 1.0.184 and libyang 2.1.148, which are used by FRR, have not presented any issues to our knowledge.
> 
> My suggestion is to install libyang3 in this PR without replacing the existing dependency.

I honestly believe not having multiple versions of libyang to be extremely important.  I think their API is stabilizing.  The only thing required was to apply some commits already upstream in FRR 10.2 to support 3.7.8.  From the commit message:
> This also backports a series of commits from FRR to support libyang3,
upgrading FRR itself isn't currently in scope:
>
> * https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/290c6e3184a8f6c4c5c39fc45dcec81508e3858b
> * https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/8e2b2caf6592b587749777f00778bf48fa164ed5
> * https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/22eccbfab916b2c6b64037e872a5c5a870d1a4d6
> * https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/commit/87c9060f90b6b9b5a69ad1e6ba6e8ebc58d94374

I think we'd be foolish to kick the can down the road while we're working on it now.   I also haven't verified if libyang2 and libyang3 can be installed simultaneously like libyang1 and libyang3 can.

Of course if you tell me there's no way you could possibly accept this PR because of this you leave me little choice but I don't see a sufficient argument at this time against it.

comments.author: bradh352
comments.body:
> Hi @bradh352 , could you help me understand why `src/sonic-yang-models/tests/yang_model_tests/tests/` is impacted? Aren't they dependent on libyang 1.0.73?

From the commit message:
> sonic-yang-models: Update test cases in preparation for libyang3
Convert some yang model test cases that use `eStr` for failure matching
to use `eStrKey` instead to standardize expected failure matching so
when messsages change they can be updated in one place instead of all
over.
>
> Also, split out some new `eStrKey` values that are needed for libyang3
due to different messages, and document the libyang3 values needed once
upgraded but keep libyang1 values for now.
>
> Finally, some tests were using both `eStr` and `eStrKey` and the `eStr`
portion is not needed to perform a meaningful validation, plus the
`eStr` in these cases are not valid for libyang3.

So basically, its just to make the review of the upgrade to libyang3 easier.   I've actually got libyang3 working and passing these test cases so I wanted a bulk of the test case changes done here to make it easier to review the more complex porting of the libyang1 python swig module to libyang3 python cffi.

comments.author: bradh352
comments.body:
> Guess I need to figure out python wheel packaging for cross compilation to support marvell armhf (its an architecture-specific package since it uses cffi)? I clearly am not testing such a use case currently in my local environment. Anyone have any pointers for this?

Looks like azure isn't actually cross compiling at all, its running an armhf image that is advertising armv8l support which I think just means the kernel knows its a 64bit cpu ... but the system was compiled for armv7l/armhf, so python is I think determining the system based on `uname -m`.

I tried using a 64bit arm vm on my macbook to build sonic, but it immediately fails as it thinks I need to use QEMU multiarch ... even hacking the makefile to disable that and it fails later on.  Parallels doesn't allow me to directly install an armhf image, so I guess I'm dead in the water trying to test this on my own hardware right now.  I might need to pick up an rpi5 or something to build but that seems like it might be really really slow....

So I'll probably try to throw in some test commits to see if a simple 'setarch armhf' works around the issue.

linkedPullRequests.title: sonic-mgmt-common: port to libyang3
linkedPullRequests.author: bradh352
linkedPullRequests.body:
SONiC Libyang3 upgrade Tracking ticket https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22385 

This PR depends on the other PRs mentioned in the above tracking ticket.

The API changes between libyang1 and libyang3 are drastic.

The cvl test cases are currently passing all tests.

This depends on libyang3's [devel](https://github.com/CESNET/libyang/tree/devel) branch plus this rejected patch:
- https://github.com/CESNET/libyang/pull/2362 -- will never be accepted upstream. libyang maintainer says sonic-yang-mgmt needs to be rearchitected, it is a bad application design to need such a flag.

Or the libyang3 package built via sonic-buildimage which is based on v3.7.8 + all the necessary patches, part of https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/21679

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22385

See comment https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt-common/pull/157#issuecomment-4463781541 for the description about supporting both libyang1 and libyang3

linkedPullRequests.author: bhouse-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### What I did

sonic-utilities should never call directly into libyang.  All functionality it needs should be provided in sonic-yang-mgmt.  This resolves issues when libyang changes API/ABI such as happened between libyang1 and libyang2, and again between libyang2 and libyang3.

Depends on https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24414 and https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/26563
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/22385

#### How I did it

Removed calls to libyang and instead uses new functionality introduced in sonic-yang-mgmt.

Also installs both libyang1 and libyang3 for tests to maintain compatibility with both during the migration.

#### How to verify it

After https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/24414 merges observe test cases still pass.

linkedPullRequests.title: [rules] Remove libyang1, keep only libyang3
linkedPullRequests.author: bhouse-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

SONiC has been migrating from libyang1 (`libyang`, `libyang-cpp`, `python3-yang`) to libyang3 (`libyang3`, `python3-libyang`) incrementally, building both in parallel during the transition. This is the **last** PR: with every consumer now on libyang3, it removes libyang1 entirely along with the transitional scaffolding that kept the two from colliding — the `libyang3-dev-done` ordering shim and the post-FRR `UNINSTALLS` of `libyang3-dev` (needed only because `libyang1-dev` and `libyang3-dev` can't be installed on the build host at once).

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22385 — this is the last PR to complete the fix.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

- Migrated the remaining consumer `rules/*.mk` and platform rules that still pulled libyang1 packages (`LIBYANG`, `LIBYANG_CPP`, `LIBYANG_PY3`, `LIBYANG_DEV`, `LIBYANG*_DBG`) to the libyang3 equivalents (`LIBYANG3`, `LIBYANG3_PY3`, `LIBYANG3_DEV`, `LIBYANG3_DBG`). The Python binding moves from `LIBYANG_PY3` (`python3-yang`, libyang1 C++ wrapper) to `LIBYANG3_PY3` (`python3-libyang`, libyang3 direct bindings); `LIBYANG_CPP` has no libyang3 equivalent and is dropped.
- Removed the `libyang3-dev-done` coexistence shim (`rules/libyang3-dev-done.{mk,dep}` and the `$(LIBYANG)_PHONIES` hook). It existed only to order builds before the conflicting `libyang1-dev` was installed; with no libyang1 consumer the constraint is gone.
- Stopped uninstalling `libyang3-dev` after the FRR build (`$(FRR)_UNINSTALLS`). It was the partner of the coexistence shim; with no `libyang1-dev` to install, stripping `libyang3-dev` broke sonic-gnmi's CGo build (`fatal error: libyang/libyang.h: No such file or directory`).
- Deleted the libyang1 build itself: `rules/libyang.{mk,dep}` and `src/libyang`.
- **Deleted the SONiC-built `libpcre3`** (`rules/libpcre3.{mk,dep}` and `src/libpcre3`). This custom PCRE **8.x** build existed *solely* as a runtime dependency of libyang1, which linked the legacy PCRE3. libyang3 links **PCRE2** (`libpcre2-8-0`, already provided by the Debian base), so no SONiC-built libpcre3 is needed. With libyang1 gone, nothing in the build graph `DEPENDS`/`RDEPENDS` on `LIBPCRE3` or any of its derived packages (`LIBPCRE16_3`, `LIBPCRE32_3`, `LIBPCRECPP0V5`, `LIBPCRE3_DEV`, `LIBPCRE3_DBG`) — it was fully orphaned.
  - **Note for reviewers:** this removes only SONiC's *custom rebuild* of PCRE 8.39. Dockers and slave images that `apt-get install libpcre3` continue to pull the **Debian distro** package (`2:8.39-15`, note the epoch) from the base repos — a different version string than the SONiC build, and unaffected by this change. The existing `versions-deb-*` lock entries for `libpcre3` reference that distro package and remain valid.
- Cleaned up stale libyang1 references: dropped the libyang1 **and `libpcre3`** debs from the `sonic-yang-models` install line in `sonic_debian_extension.j2`, and removed `/src/libyang/` from `CODEOWNERS`. The `libpcre3_*.deb` glob on that install line was only there to satisfy libyang1; once libpcre3 stopped being built it became a dangling reference that broke image assembly with `cp: cannot stat 'target/debs/trixie/libpcre3_*.deb': No such file or directory`.

#### How to verify it

- `make configure PLATFORM=<vendor>` followed by a full image build completes; libyang1 debs (`libyang_*`, `libyang-cpp_*`, `python3-yang_*`) and the SONiC-built `libpcre3_*` debs are no longer produced or installed.
- `grep -rn 'LIBYANG[^3]'` over `rules/` and the build templates returns no libyang1 make-variable references; `git grep LIBPCRE3` returns no SONiC build rules (only distro `versions-deb-*` lock entries remain).
- sonic-gnmi / sonic-mgmt-common (CVL) build successfully — `libyang/libyang.h` remains present at FRR-and-later build stages.

#### Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)

- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511

#### Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)

- [ ] <!-- image version 1 -->
- [ ] <!-- image version 2 -->

#### Description for the changelog

Remove libyang1; migrate all remaining consumers to libyang3 and delete the libyang1 build, the SONiC-built libpcre3 (a libyang1-only dependency), and the coexistence shims.

#### Link to config_db schema for YANG module changes

N/A — build-system only; no YANG model or config_db schema changes.
